entries.lesson_title: Time-Shifting Property of the Laplace Transform
entries.core_move: Apply the one-sided Laplace time-shifting property to convert delayed signals written as $f(t-a)u(t-a)$ into $e^{-as}F(s)$ so unit-step and piecewise-signal transforms can be handled algebraically.
Convert a delayed waveform into $f(t-a)u(t-a)$ by identifying the delay $a$ and shifted local time so the one-sided Laplace time-shifting property can be applied to piecewise signal representations.
Convert each shifted unit step $u(t-a)$ into the Laplace-domain factor $e^{-as}/s$, interpreting the exponential factor as the delay marker used in piecewise-signal transforms.
Rewrite shifted ramp terms as delayed ramp-and-step components and apply the Laplace time-shifting property to compute their transforms for piecewise-signal representations.

entries.lesson_title: Rewriting Piecewise Signals with Unit Steps
entries.core_move: Rewrite each piecewise continuous-time signal as an initial expression plus breakpoint-triggered unit-step corrections, converting every later segment into a shifted form suitable for applying the Laplace time-shifting property.

Compute one-sided Laplace transforms of piecewise continuous-time signals by converting interval definitions into shifted unit-step terms and applying linearity with the Laplace time-shifting property.
